decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Mega Gengar. Lead Gengar and Aerodactyl to control turn one against sun or spread offense using Wide Guard and fast Shadow Tag pressure. Dragonite and Arcanine in the back offer priority, Intimidate, and strong physical coverage to clean up remaining threats.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has Sun core (Mega Charizard Y + Focus Sash Venusaur), Scarf Garchomp, Life Orb Primarina, Leftovers Goodra-Hisui, Charti Talonflame. Plan: Mega Gengar + Aerodactyl lead traps and mitigates Charizard/Garchomp spread options via Wide Guard; Dragonite and Arcanine backline provides priority and stat suppression.

decisions.rationale: Intend Mega Charizard Y. Charizard/Venusaur establish sun immediately: Venusaur can act ahead of Aero and Mega Gengar while Charizard attacks or protects from Rock Slide lines. Scarf Garchomp gives immediate Rock/Ground cleanup and Primarina supplies the Dragonite/Krookodile endgame; this preserves a fast sun mode without relying on Tailwind.
decisions.notebook: Opponent roster: Mega Gengar (Timid, Shadow Tag after Mega), Focus Sash Aerodactyl with Rock Slide/Wide Guard/Tailwind/Taunt, LO Dragonite, Sitrus Intimidate Arcanine, Leftovers Clefable, Scarf Intimidate Krookodile. Primary game-plan remains Mega Charizard Y + Chlorophyll Venusaur; respect Aerodactyl Wide Guard and Rock Slide, plus Mega Gengar trapping. Garchomp and Primarina are preferred cleanup into Aero/Arcanine and Dragonite/Krookodile respectively.

decisions.rationale: Aerodactyl outspeeds base Charizard and threatens a 4x super-effective Rock Slide (83.8-158.8%), which can OHKO Charizard Y before it acts. Gengar is vulnerable to Ground-type attacks from both foes (Scorching Sands, Earth Power), so Protect + Mega Evolve guarantees Gengar's safety while activating Shadow Tag to trap both targets. Aerodactyl's Focus Sash and typing protect it from single-target OHKOs on Turn 1.
decisions.notebook: Opponent: Sun core (Mega Charizard Y + Focus Sash Venusaur), Scarf Garchomp, LO Primarina, Leftovers Goodra-H, Charti Talonflame. Plan: Mega Gengar + Aerodactyl lead traps and mitigates Charizard/Garchomp options.

decisions.rationale: Mega Y activates sun, giving Venusaur Chlorophyll speed to put Aerodactyl to sleep before Rock Slide, while Charizard threatens the immediate super-effective KO on Mega Gengar. This covers Tailwind and Rock Slide more cleanly than attacking Aerodactyl through its Sash/Wide Guard options.
decisions.notebook: Opponent may use Aerodactyl Wide Guard/Tailwind as Mega Gengar establishes Shadow Tag. Preserve the Charizard Y + Chlorophyll Venusaur mode when possible; prioritize denying Aerodactyl Rock Slide/Tailwind, then leverage Ground attacks into Gengar. Garchomp remains useful against Aerodactyl/Arcanine; Primarina is reserved for Dragonite/Krookodile cleanup.

decisions.rationale: Gengar is heavily threatened by Venusaur's fast Earth Power and Charizard Y's Scorching Sands, and Protect has reduced accuracy after turn 1. Aerodactyl is asleep and cannot use Wide Guard. Switching Gengar to Dragonite safely absorbs incoming Ground attacks via Flying typing while resisting Fire/Grass, while Aerodactyl burns a sleep turn taking minimal or zero damage.

Both targeted Ground attacks bypass a potential waking Aerodactyl Wide Guard and should remove Mega Gengar together if it does not land consecutive Protect. Venusaur is guaranteed faster than Gengar, and this line denies Gengar an attack on failed Protect while preserving Focus Sash against Sludge Bomb.
decisions.notebook: Mega Gengar has revealed Protect; its next consecutive Protect has reduced success. Aerodactyl carries Focus Sash, Unnerve, Rock Slide, Wide Guard, Tailwind, and Taunt. Maintain targeted attacks when Aerodactyl can use Wide Guard; Garchomp is the preferred Aerodactyl/Arcanine answer and Primarina the Dragonite/Krookodile cleanup mode.

decisions.rationale: Primarina avoids giving Dragonite a free 4x Ice Spinner target and immediately supports the Dragonite matchup with Ice Beam or Moonblast. Garchomp remains the cleaner for Aerodactyl and Arcanine once Dragonite is handled.
decisions.notebook: Mega Gengar has revealed Protect; a consecutive Protect is less reliable. Aerodactyl: Focus Sash, Unnerve, Rock Slide, Wide Guard, Tailwind, Taunt. Avoid relying on spread damage while Aerodactyl can Wide Guard; use targeted attacks or preserve Garchomp. Primarina is preferred Dragonite/Krookodile cleanup; Garchomp is the Aerodactyl/Arcanine answer.

decisions.rationale: Primarina threatens a 4x super-effective Ice Beam on Dragonite, while Chlorophyll Venusaur outspeeds Dragonite in Sun. Using Protect on Dragonite safely negates incoming targeted attacks. Aerodactyl at full HP with Focus Sash uses Rock Slide to chip Venusaur into guaranteed ESpeed KO range while pressuring Primarina and fishing for flinches.

Ice Beam is a guaranteed targeted OHKO on Dragonite and ignores Aerodactyl's Wide Guard. Venusaur cannot safely act through Dragonite's priority ExtremeSpeed or Ice Spinner, the latter being a guaranteed KO, so Protect preserves it and avoids giving Dragonite a free removal. If Dragonite Protects, Primarina remains healthy for the next attempt.
decisions.notebook: Aerodactyl has Focus Sash, Unnerve, Rock Slide, Wide Guard, Tailwind, and Taunt. Mega Gengar revealed Protect. Avoid relying on spread damage while Aerodactyl can Wide Guard; targeted attacks are preferred. Primarina is preferred Dragonite/Krookodile cleanup; preserve Garchomp as the Aerodactyl/Arcanine answer. Dragonite carries Life Orb, Inner Focus, ExtremeSpeed, Ice Spinner, Rock Slide, Protect; Ice Spinner is lethal to Venusaur.

decisions.rationale: Primarina's Ice Beam threatens a 4x OHKO on Dragonite. Dragonite's Extreme Speed (+2 priority) combined with Aerodactyl's high Speed (200) Rock Slide double-targets Primarina before it can move (80-112 Speed), heavily favoring a KO on 56% HP Primarina before it can attack. Rock Slide also chips Venusaur and offers flinch chance.

Switching preserves Primarina from the guaranteed ExtremeSpeed KO while Venusaur, faster in sun, can put Dragonite to sleep before Ice Spinner. This retains Primarina to immediately threaten Dragonite with Ice Beam later and avoids relying on Venusaur's reduced-success Protect.

selection: Wide Guard (your side, including ally Dragonite)
decisions.rationale: Wide Guard (+3 priority) safely blocks Garchomp's expected spread move (Rock Slide/Earthquake) and prevents a combined double-hit KO on Aerodactyl. Dragonite's Extreme Speed (+2 priority) will immediately KO Venusaur (29% HP) if Dragonite wakes up this turn, before Venusaur or Scarf Garchomp act. If Dragonite remains asleep, Aerodactyl preserves its Focus Sash and outspeeds Venusaur on Turn 6 once Sun expires.
decisions.notebook: Opponent: Sun core (Mega Charizard Y + Focus Sash Venusaur), Scarf Garchomp, LO Primarina, Leftovers Goodra-H, Charti Talonflame.

decisions.rationale: Switching in Arcanine triggers Intimidate on Scarf Garchomp (locked into Dragon Claw), drastically cutting its physical output and allowing Arcanine to comfortably absorb the hit with Sitrus Berry recovery. This keeps Gengar-Mega healthy in reserve and gives Arcanine immediate priority pressure with Extreme Speed against 29% HP Venusaur next turn.
decisions.notebook: Opponent: Sun core (Mega Charizard Y + Focus Sash Venusaur), Scarf Garchomp (locked Dragon Claw), LO Primarina, Leftovers Goodra-H, Charti Talonflame.

decisions.rationale: Target Dragonite with the guaranteed super-effective Dragon Claw while shielding Venusaur from Rock Slide and Ice Spinner. Dragonite’s wake-up Extreme Speed is the main failure point, but Rock Slide is unreliable into Aerodactyl’s possible Wide Guard and cannot secure Dragonite through its Focus Sash-free bulk as cleanly.

Garchomp is Choice-locked into Dragon Claw at -1 Attack, posing minimal threat. Venusaur is at 29% HP. Arcanine's priority +2 Extreme Speed combined with Aerodactyl's fast Rock Slide (200 Speed) guarantees Venusaur is KOed before it can use Sleep Powder or attack. Rock Slide also chips Garchomp while Venusaur's Protect has a reduced success rate after consecutive use.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Arcanine is strongly incentivized to pivot to Gengar against Earth Power. Dragon Claw into its slot punishes that switch, while Venusaur’s Protect covers both Flare Blitz and Rock Slide if it succeeds. If Arcanine stays, it takes Dragon Claw and remains in range for Venusaur’s Earth Power next turn. Garchomp is guaranteed ahead of Aerodactyl.

Garchomp is Scarf-locked into Dragon Claw. Venusaur is at 29% HP and Protect has failed/been used heavily. Combining Arcanine's +2 priority Extreme Speed (15.5-29.7%) with Aerodactyl's 200 Speed Rock Slide (20.3-37.4%) guarantees Venusaur is KO'd before it can move, even on minimum damage rolls, neutralizing any Sleep Powder threat before Gengar enters to lock down Garchomp and Primarina with Shadow Tag.

Venusaur is in guaranteed Extreme Speed KO range and its repeated Protect is unreliable. Switching preserves it and brings Primarina in while Garchomp’s locked Dragon Claw applies immediate damage to Arcanine. Do not rely on Rock Slide through Aerodactyl’s known Wide Guard.
decisions.notebook: Aerodactyl: Focus Sash, Unnerve, Rock Slide, Wide Guard, Tailwind, Taunt. Mega Gengar has Protect. Dragonite: Life Orb, Inner Focus, Extreme Speed, Ice Spinner, Rock Slide, Protect. Arcanine: Sitrus Berry, Intimidate, Flare Blitz, Extreme Speed, Will-O-Wisp, Snarl. Avoid spread attacks while Aerodactyl can Wide Guard; targeted attacks preferred. Primarina is preferred cleanup into Dragonite/Krookodile; preserve Garchomp as an Aerodactyl/Arcanine answer.

decisions.rationale: Arcanine's Extreme Speed (+2 priority) acts before Scarf Garchomp and Primarina, removing Primarina (3% HP) before it can move. Scarf Garchomp is locked into Dragon Claw at -1 Atk and cannot KO Arcanine (53% HP). Aerodactyl's Rock Slide chips Garchomp to ~20% HP and guarantees that Aerodactyl (200 Speed) outspeeds incoming Venusaur (29% HP, 100-132 Speed) on the following turn to finish the match.

Protect denies Arcanine's immediate Extreme Speed KO on Primarina while Scarf Garchomp removes Arcanine before Aerodactyl acts. This is the only line that clears Arcanine without voluntarily sacrificing Primarina to priority; it retains the best Rock Slide-miss path into the Aerodactyl endgame.
decisions.notebook: Aerodactyl is Focus Sash Unnerve with Rock Slide, Wide Guard, Tailwind, and Taunt; do not rely on spread damage into it. Mega Gengar has Protect. Dragonite was Life Orb Inner Focus with Extreme Speed, Ice Spinner, Rock Slide, Protect. Arcanine is Sitrus Berry Intimidate with Flare Blitz, Extreme Speed, Will-O-Wisp, Snarl. Preserve targeted attacks against Aerodactyl and respect Extreme Speed cleanup from Arcanine.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp is at 18% HP and choice-locked into Dragon Claw. Arcanine's +2 priority Extreme Speed into Garchomp deals 11.6-25.1% damage, guaranteeing that combined with Aerodactyl's Rock Slide (7.0-15.8% into Garchomp), Garchomp is KOed before it can move next turn. Rock Slide also KOs 3% HP Primarina simultaneously. Even if Garchomp attacks first after Espeed, its -1 Dragon Claw deals ~23% to 55% HP Arcanine, leaving both our active Pokémon healthy to win the turn.
decisions.notebook: Opponent team: Sun core (Mega Charizard Y + Focus Sash Venusaur), Scarf Garchomp (locked Dragon Claw), LO Primarina, Leftovers Goodra-H, Charti Talonflame.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Scarf Garchomp is guaranteed ahead of Aerodactyl and Dragon Claw has already put Arcanine in KO range, removing its priority cleanup. Primarina cannot safely attack through Extreme Speed; consecutive Protect is the only line that can preserve it from Aerodactyl’s Rock Slide after Arcanine falls. Switching Venusaur simply exposes it to Extreme Speed or Rock Slide.
decisions.notebook: Aerodactyl is Focus Sash Unnerve with Rock Slide, Wide Guard, Tailwind, and Taunt; use targeted attacks rather than relying on spread damage. Mega Gengar has Protect and is Timid. Dragonite was Life Orb Inner Focus with Extreme Speed, Ice Spinner, Rock Slide, Protect. Arcanine is Sitrus Berry Intimidate with Flare Blitz, Extreme Speed, Will-O-Wisp, Snarl. Preserve targeted attacks against Aerodactyl and respect Extreme Speed cleanup from Arcanine.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Extreme Speed (+2 priority) into Venusaur deals 14.4-32.9%. Aerodactyl (200 Speed) outspeeds both foes and uses Rock Slide, dealing 18.2-41.9% to Venusaur and >10% to Primarina. Combined damage on Venusaur (32.6-74.8%) guarantees a KO on its 29% HP (Sash is inactive below 100%), while Rock Slide guarantees the KO on 3% HP Primarina before either foe can move.
decisions.notebook: Opponent team: Sun core (Mega Charizard Y + Focus Sash Venusaur), Scarf Garchomp, LO Primarina, Leftovers Goodra-H, Charti Talonflame.

decisions.rationale: Targeted double attacks are the only line that can immediately remove Arcanine and Aerodactyl. Earth Power is a guaranteed KO on Arcanine, while Life Orb Ice Beam guarantees Aerodactyl’s Focus Sash activation. Primarina is vulnerable to Extreme Speed, but repeated Protect is heavily reduced and offers less immediate upside.

reflections.summary: The bring of Aerodactyl and Arcanine successfully neutralized the opponent's Scarf Garchomp and weakened Sun attackers through Intimidate, chip damage, and Extreme Speed priority late-game.
reflections.adjustment: Prevent Venusaur's Sleep Powder from disabling key attackers early by utilizing Aerodactyl's Taunt or Gengar's pressure before Sun is set up.
reflections.notebook: Opponent sets: Mega Charizard Y, Modest Chlorophyll Venusaur (Focus Sash; Sleep Powder, Earth Power, Sludge Bomb), Jolly Scarf Garchomp (Dragon Claw, Earthquake, Rock Slide, Poison Jab), Modest Life Orb Primarina (Liquid Voice, Protect). Goodra-H and Talonflame left on bench. Plan: Maintain Aerodactyl + Arcanine priority/speed control core; use Taunt to shut down Venusaur's status moves.

reflections.summary: Lost because Aerodactyl and Arcanine remained intact for the endgame: Aerodactyl’s Rock Slide pressure and Arcanine’s Extreme Speed repeatedly forced defensive lines, while Aerodactyl was never meaningfully damaged. The Charizard-Y/Venusaur-oriented four and Mega choice were poorly suited to an Aerodactyl-led matchup with Wide Guard and Rock Slide.
reflections.adjustment: For game 2, do not default to the Charizard-Y/Venusaur package into Aerodactyl; prioritize a four that can immediately threaten Aerodactyl with targeted damage while retaining a healthy answer to Arcanine’s Extreme Speed cleanup.
reflections.notebook: Aerodactyl is Focus Sash Unnerve with Rock Slide, Wide Guard, Tailwind, and Taunt; it can enable Arcanine endgames if left unchecked, so prioritize targeted pressure into it rather than spread moves. Mega Gengar has Protect and is Timid. Dragonite was Life Orb Inner Focus with Extreme Speed, Ice Spinner, Rock Slide, Protect. Arcanine is Sitrus Berry Intimidate with Flare Blitz, Extreme Speed, Will-O-Wisp, Snarl; preserve a healthy Pokémon that can withstand or deter its priority cleanup. Reconsider Charizard-Y/Venusaur as the default Mega/package versus this Aerodactyl-Arcanine structure.
